key_insight: A graph neural network trained on smaller GW calculations predicts quasiparticle energy levels in large supercells at a fraction of the computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make accurate electronic-structure calculations more practical for defects, surfaces, and moiré systems where conventional GW becomes costly.
method: Represent atoms as graph nodes and interatomic distances as edges.
Use DFT wavefunction projections onto localized atomic orbitals as input features.
Build a targeted, compact GW training dataset and optimize hyperparameters with Bayesian optimization.
evidence_signal: For monolayer MoS₂ with a sulfur vacancy, the abstract reports mean absolute errors of 10–50 meV.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on representative GW training data; transferability beyond the reported MoS₂ vacancy case is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Graph Neural Networks for Accurate Quasiparticle Energy Levels in Large Supercells of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
